subject: Medicover security discovery — audit trail export & immutability questions
messages:
From: Alex Geller <alex.geller@medicover.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medicover.com>, Medicover SecOps <secops@medicover.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from today's demo — audit trail & write-once requirements

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — product looked promising. My SecOps and procurement partners asked me to consolidate a few follow-ups related to audit logging and immutability so we can move the security review forward. High-level items: 

- SOC 2 status: do you have a recent Type II report, and what systems are in-scope?
- Data protection: GDPR/HIPAA applicability (we have PHI in scope) and any required BAAs?
- Admin activity logs: what events are captured (user creation, role changes, API key usage, token issuance/revocation, policy changes), retention defaults, and ability to filter/search by user or request id.
- API call logs: request/response metadata, latencies, error codes — can these be exported in bulk?
- Exportability & format: bulk exports (S3 / JSONL / CSV), incremental vs full snapshot, ability to provide a tamper-evident hash for exported batches.
- Immutability / WORM: do you offer write-once options for audit archives (hosted or via customer-managed S3 object lock), and how do you demonstrate chain-of-custody?

I attached a short spreadsheet with our initial VSQ items. Could you confirm who on your side will take point for the VSQ and whether you can produce a small sample of admin/API logs (sanitized) so our SecOps team can validate fields and formats?

Target timing: procurement would like to close technical review this month to stay on our Q4 deployment plan.

Appreciate the help — happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Alex
Alex Geller
Director, Platform Security
Medicover Health

Attachment: medicover-vsq-questions.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12 rows)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Geller <alex.geller@medicover.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — audit trail & write-once requirements

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list and the attached VSQ. Below is a concise answer set and proposed next steps; I copied Ava (AE) and Dylan (Product Ops) to handle technical deliverables.

Quick answers: 
- SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report covering our hosted inference control plane and production serving runtime (report issued 2025-11). We can provide the SOC 2 Management Assertion and the full report under NDA; production logs and Dedicated/Private deployments have separate scoping notes (we enumerate these in the attestation appendix).
- GDPR/HIPAA & BAAs: We support GDPR controls; for HIPAA we offer BAAs for Dedicated and Private deployments (on-hosted customers require additional configuration). For hosted customers handling PHI at scale, we recommend our Private deployment.
- Admin activity logs: We capture user lifecycle events, API token lifecycle, role/permission changes, configuration rollouts, model rollouts, and policy overrides. Default retention for hosted is 90 days; retention can be extended for Dedicated and Private (customer-configurable). Logs include timestamps (RFC3339), actor id, request id, request path, outcome (success/error code), and payload metadata (truncated).
- API logs & export: We provide bulk export via the Console (CSV/JSONL) and an export API that can write to customer S3. Exports are incremental (cursor-based) and full-snapshot capable.
- Immutability: For hosted customers we provide signed export bundles (SHA256 manifest) and server-side append-only storage for the duration of retention. For Dedicated/Private you can enable customer-managed S3 object lock (WORM) and we recommend enabling Glacier Vault Lock or equivalent for longer-term archival. We can produce a signed chain-of-custody record for each export.

Next steps / proposed MAP (mutual action plan):
1) You share the VSQ (received) — thanks.
2) We will return an annotated VSQ and a small sanitized admin/API log sample for Medicover to validate fields (target: 48–72 hours).
3) If required, set a short technical call between your SecOps and our infra team (Dylan) for any field-level clarifications.

Ava / Dylan — can you confirm you can produce a redacted log sample and the VSQ annotation by EOD Thu 8/7? Also flag any items that require engineering sign-off (I expect immutability implementation details may need a short write-up).

Alex — happy to jump on a 30m call if that helps expedite procurement. If you can confirm the deployment type you expect (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) that will help clarify retention/BAA options.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 6 Aug 2026 08:20:00 -0700

Quick internal sync — action items for our side:
- Dylan: generate a 1MB sanitized admin+API log sample (JSONL) and a short readme describing each field. Attach screenshot of Console export settings. (Due: Thu 8/7, EOD)
- Rishi: draft annotated VSQ answers for security controls (SOC 2 in-scope list, encryption at rest/in transit, key management, access reviews). Note any items that need legal/eng escalation. (Due: Thu 8/7, noon)
- Kimberly: I will coordinate the NDA and attach the SOC 2 assertion to the response if the customer requests it.

One-liner replies to expected tricky asks: we do support retention extension and customer-managed immutability (for Dedicated/Private) — those need sales ops + infra involvement but are standard for enterprise deals.

Ava
AE, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Geller <alex.geller@medicover.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — audit trail & write-once requirements

Hi Alex — thanks for the patience. Per our MAP, attached are: (1) a sanitized 1MB admin+API log sample (redwood-admin-logs-sample.txt), (2) an annotated VSQ draft (we returned the spreadsheet with inline answers), and (3) a screenshot of Console export settings. Key clarifications in the attached answers:

- SOC 2: we can share the Type II report under NDA; the report scope includes control plane, serving runtime, and observability pipelines (production).
- PHI handling: Hosted customers should avoid sending raw PHI; Dedicated/Private are the recommended deployment models for BAA support. We can start BAA discussions in parallel.
- Export immutability options: hosted exports come with SHA256 manifests and signed delivery. For long-term WORM you can configure Dedicated/Private exports to your S3 bucket using object lock (we've done this with several customers).

On the logs sample: fields included are timestamp, actor_id (redacted), request_id, endpoint, http_status, duration_ms, change_type, resource_id, and change_summary. Let us know if you need additional fields or a different format (CSV/Parquet).

If the SecOps team is satisfied with the formats, procurement can proceed; otherwise suggest a 30-min technical deep dive with Dylan and Rishi next week.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-admin-logs-sample.txt (sanitized, 1MB JSONL), medicover-vsq-questions-annotated.xlsx (VSQ with inline answers), screenshot-log-config.png
